title: Lean Mass Gains, Cardiac Remodeling, and Muscle Oxidative Changes With High-Dose Salbutamol During Resistance Training: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Hostrup M, Jessen S, Tischer SG, Kalsen A, Hadad R, Bonde PL, et al.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
population: Healthy trained men aged about 23 years in a supervised full-body resistance training programme three times a week; oral salbutamol 16 mg/day or placebo, double-blind; 26 completed
funder: The study was supported by an independent research grant from World Anti-Doping Agency (Grant 11D5VB).
authorConflicts: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
result: Lean mass rose 1.8 kg more with salbutamol than placebo (95% CI 0.5 to 3.1). Cardiac magnetic resonance showed no between-group difference in cardiac structure or function, including left ventricular mass, whereas echocardiography showed greater posterior, septal and relative wall thickness with salbutamol (p < 0.01). Time to exhaustion in cardiopulmonary exercise testing increased 7% with placebo and not with salbutamol; muscle capillary density and citrate synthase and 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activities fell with salbutamol (p < 0.01). The dose was supratherapeutic and the participants were healthy men.
